newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian party wants bank foreign-share details.
newsitem.headline: Australian party wants bank foreign-share details.

text.p: The Australian Democrats, a leftist minor party holding key votes in parliament, called on the government on Wednesday to issue a policy statement to clarify its stance on foreign investment in banking.

Democrats leader Cheryl Kernot also welcomed Treasurer Peter Costello's statement that he would not allow mergers between Australia's "Big Four" banks, which formed part of his response to the Wallis Report on the financial sector.

"The Wallis Report itself recommends that a significant increase in foreign ownership in the banking sector would be contrary to the public interest, and I believe that the Treasurer now needs to issue a clear policy statement setting limits to foreign shareholding in banks to deny control of Austrlian banks to foreign interests," she said in a statement.

Earlier, Costello said in a partial response to the report -- the Financial System Inquiry -- that he would remove the blanket ban on foreign takeovers of Australian banks but would still oppose large-scale acquisitions by foreigners.
He did not, however, say exactly what that meant -- although he did say foreign participation in the sector could not reach the 60 percent level that applied in print media.
Foreign banks have been able to operate in Australia through their own subsidiaries since the financial markets were deregulated in the mid 1980s.

The Democrats can be important to any government policy that needs new legislation or regulation, because the ruling Liberal-National coalition is two votes short of a majority in the Senate, the upper house of parliament.
But the government can change many policies without legislation, because the office of Treasurer is already invested with such powers as a veto over bank mergers and acquisitions.
Costello said the government would detail its full government response to the Wallis Report after the May 13 budget.
The big four banks are National Australia Bank Ltd, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Westpac Banking Corp and Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd .
